questions.explanation: CRUD stands for Create, Read, Update and Delete, the basic functions used in any database for structured data.
CRAP stands for Create, Replicate, Append and Process, describing how high-velocity non-transactional data is handled.

questions.stem: To which type of data do the CRUD functions apply?
options: Structured data in databases used for the last few decades
questions.explanation: CRUD describes the create, read, update and delete functions used with structured data in any database over the last few decades.

questions.stem: Which of these sources is given as an example of high-velocity CRAP data?
options: Web logs, social streams, CCTV, sensor data and mobile data
questions.explanation: The new era's data flows in with high velocity from web logs, social streams, CCTV, sensor data, videos, social media, mobile and geo-spatial sources.

questions.stem: Why is CRAP data normally not updated or deleted?
options: Because it is stored on read-only media
Because it is too small to matter
Because of the speed at which it arrives, so it is only created, replicated, appended and processed
questions.explanation: The speed this data is coming at means it is normally not possible to update or delete it, so it is created, replicated, appended and processed only.

questions.stem: How was the non-transactional data of the new era originally regarded?
options: As CRAP data, because it had nothing to do with transactional data
As the most valuable asset from the start
questions.explanation: All this data had nothing to do with transactional data, so it used to be called CRAP data.

questions.stem: How is CRAP data regarded now?
options: As worthless noise to be discarded
As one of the most valuable assets of any organisation
As data that must be deleted within a day
As data reserved for archival only
questions.explanation: Although once called CRAP data, this data has now become one of the most valuable assets of any organisation.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT one of the CRUD operations?
questions.explanation: Replicate belongs to CRAP; the CRUD operations are Create, Read, Update and Delete.

questions.stem: Which operation appears in both CRUD and CRAP?
questions.explanation: Create is the C in both CRUD (Create, Read, Update, Delete) and CRAP (Create, Replicate, Append, Process).

questions.stem: Which operation replaces Update and Delete when handling high-velocity CRAP data?
questions.explanation: Because the data cannot practically be updated or deleted, it is created, replicated, appended and processed only.
